answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the economy binds node registration to a dynamic stake-slashing protocol. An agent must anchor its cryptographic identity across a verifiable graph trellis, burning stake that scales superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^{1.5}$ for $n$ identities controlled. Under this economic friction, an attacker pushing identity creation toward a mass-scale horizon faces exponential cost spikes, leaving the network stable as an opal.
